intro.title: Hi, I'm Terrorschiki
intro.desc: Focused on quadruped robot reinforcement learning, SLAM localization, and embedded systems — with awards including a ROBOCON National Second Prize and a Physical AI Hackathon track championship.

item0.title: Quadruped Robot RL Gait Training & Navigation
item0.desc: Quadruped gait trained with the Robot_lab framework and deployed via RL_sar for Sim2Real; features a customized GLIM odometry, art-planner 2.5D elevation-map navigation, and a self-developed local planner with low compute requirements. Won the National Second Prize in ROBOCON Bio-inspired Legged Robots, and was invited by the ROBOCON committee to represent Bilibili at the WAIC World AI Conference flash event.

item1.title: SkylandX C01 LiDAR ROS2 Driver & IMU Calibration Tools
item1.desc: A lightweight LiDAR driver built on raw UDP communication — unpacks data, publishes point clouds in PointCloud2 format, and outputs IMU data in m/s² SI units, with no complex SDK dependency. Includes a one-click IMU calibration script based on the kailbr project, improving LiDAR odometry accuracy by 300% (closed-loop test with GLIM). Planned open-source release after October stability tests.

item2.title: Four-IMU Reinforcement Learning Exoskeleton
item2.desc: Local agent deployment and communication framework on the SpacemiT K3 dev board; an improved EpsonG354 driver with multi-IMU hardware binding and hot-swappable topics, fusing ESKF + Mahony for IMU attitude — providing fine-grained pose data for RL motion control; a one-click motor homing program for Lingzu RS02 motors. Won the ALLOPO Track Championship at the Physical AI Hackathon.

item3.title: GLIM-based Robot Localization System
item3.desc: GLIM odometry with real-time mapping output and GPU acceleration; offline point-cloud optimization and segmentation feed the relocalization module; the Small-GICP relocalization module delivers high-precision point-cloud relocalization on a modest compute budget, correcting the robot's pose in real time. Accuracy surpasses the closed-source Odin1 algorithm, achieving 1cm accuracy in RC arenas. Nominated for the DJI ROBOCON AWARD (Technical Track).

item4.title: Gitea-based Lab Intranet Management System
item4.desc: Intranet version management based on Gitea, handling version control and inter-team collaboration for large files such as SolidWorks/STL; an Ubuntu-based NAS provides multi-redundant backups of important files. Achieves over 10x the upload/download rates of competing products, with more rigorous Git-based version management. Nominated for the DJI ROBOCON AWARD (Management Track).

item5.title: RK3588-based Intelligent Omni Steer-Wheel AGV
item5.desc: Cartographer-based 2D LiDAR SLAM and localization with indoor relocalization error under 5cm; autonomous navigation via ROS2 Navigation for the steer-wheel platform; YOLO flame and parcel detection on the RK3588 NPU, with pipeline optimizations doubling inference speed (200% of baseline). Won the National Second Prize in the Embedded Chip & System Design Competition.

item0.title: We Built a Four-DOF RL Exoskeleton at the Physical AI Hackathon — Track Champion!
item0.desc: A demo of the four-IMU reinforcement learning exoskeleton: from sensor communication framework to RL motion control, winning the ALLOPO Track Championship at the Physical AI Hackathon.

item1.title: A Student Snagged a $1,500 3D LiDAR (VLP-16) for Under $70 — Dud or Best Value Pick?
item1.desc: A second-hand Velodyne VLP-16 16-channel 3D LiDAR, originally priced in the thousands of dollars, tested end to end: teardown and build quality, point-cloud quality, and power/interface checks — with a verdict on whether students should buy one.

item2.title: Two $4 Depth Cameras Compared: Which One Is Better for Students?
item2.desc: A head-to-head look at two budget depth cameras around the 30 RMB mark — imaging quality, depth accuracy, and SDK usability — plus advice for students getting started. The matching drivers and workspace are open-sourced and ready to clone.

item3.title: This RL Project Is Wild: A Usable Model Trained in 51 Seconds!
item3.desc: A walkthrough of a new RL training framework: a usable model in just 51 seconds, covering environment setup, launching training, and running the resulting policy on hardware.

event0.title: South China University of Technology | B.Eng. in Artificial Intelligence
event0.desc: School of Future Technology. Focus areas: LiDAR localization and navigation, robot control and reinforcement learning, ROS 2 development.

event1.title: Physical AI Hackathon 2026 | Multi-IMU Four-DOF Multi-Mode Exoskeleton
event1.desc: Core team member. Improved the Epson G354 driver to output attitude via Mahony + ESKF with hot-swap support (driver and PCB carrier board open-sourced); deployed the ROS 2 environment and local agent communication on a SpacemiT K3 (RISC-V) board; wrote one-click motor homing/zero-restore scripts for the Lingzu motors. Won the ALLOPO Track Championship.

event2.title: Invited to the WAIC 2026 Pop-Up Event
event2.desc: Invited by the ROBOCON organizing committee to represent Bilibili at the WAIC (World Artificial Intelligence Conference) pop-up event, exhibiting the Robotic Lab's self-developed RL quadruped robot dog.

event3.title: ROBOCON 2026 "kongfumaster" & Bionic Legged Robot | Deputy Captain
event3.desc: Achieved 1cm closed-loop localization accuracy in the arena with GLIM and a Mid-360 LiDAR, surpassing Liuxing Technology's closed-source Odin1, winning the National First Prize in the Skills Challenge; used small-gicp for point-cloud segmentation, map reconstruction, and relocalization to win the National Second Prize in the elimination rounds; contributed to the sim-to-real transfer of RL_sar and LiDAR navigation/obstacle avoidance for the robot dog, winning the National Second Prize in that track.

event4.title: SCUT Robotic Robotics Lab | Deputy Captain
event4.desc: Responsible for R&D and personnel management of the lab's robotics projects; built and maintained the local IsaacLab RL server, NAS, and local network, and deployed Gitea for version management of SolidWorks projects and code; published 4 Bilibili videos in the 2026 season (best one exceeding 14k views) and 4+ WeChat articles, and hosted more than 5 company visits.

event5.title: Invited as a Guest Speaker to the RC Annual Conference
event5.desc: Invited as a guest to the RC Annual Conference, where I shared on host-computer performance optimization and analysis as well as LiDAR technology roadmap decisions, and exchanged technical solutions and competition organization experience with robotics teams from other universities.

event6.title: ROBOCON 2025 "Basketball" & Bionic Legged Robot Project
event6.desc: Responsible for part of the robot dog's IsaacLab RL training and host-computer performance tuning, raising the control frequency of the locomotion policy (National First Prize); deployed the 2D LiDAR field localization and visual localization solutions and built a steering-wheel chassis simulation in IsaacSim (National Third Prize). Also won a provincial Third Prize in the National Undergraduate Embedded Chip and System Design Competition.

event7.title: Invention Patent: "An Object Sorting Robot" (ZL202610627849.4)
event7.desc: Responsible for the host computer calling a depth camera to recognize and segment objects with OpenCV and issuing sorting commands; trained a YOLO model for object recognition and accelerated/quantized it with TensorRT on an Orin Nano.

event8.title: National Undergraduate Embedded Chip and System Design Competition | RK3588 Omnidirectional Steer-Wheel AGV
event8.desc: Core developer. Deployed YOLOv8 on the RK3588 NPU with traditional vision algorithms for flame detection and QR code recognition; implemented autonomous navigation based on the ROS 2 Navigation framework, fusing 2D LiDAR and gyroscope data. Won the National Second Prize.

event9.title: SCUT Hongping Changqing Scholarship
event9.desc: Awarded the South China University of Technology Hongping Changqing Scholarship.

event10.title: RAICOM AIROBOT Competition | Team Captain
event10.desc: Built a synthetic dataset with IsaacSim and combined it with real data to train YOLOv8 via the NVIDIA TAO Toolkit; implemented point-to-point navigation and autonomous obstacle avoidance for a differential-drive robot with ROS 1 Navigation. Won the National First Prize and the National Runner-Up.

event11.title: Hong Kong Young Technology Talent Exhibition and Competition (YEPC) | Undergraduate Runner-Up
event11.desc: Project "Travel Guard: AI-Enhanced Travel Belt for the Blind" — a voice-interactive smart travel system on STM32MP135 with five modules: sidewalk detection, obstacle and traffic-light recognition, Baidu API voice interaction with streamed ChatGPT dialogue, Amap GPS positioning, and MPU6050 + SVM fall detection. Won the undergraduate Runner-Up Prize and was covered on SCUT's WeChat official account.
